text.title: Use Case Mapping Core Rules
text.summary: 6 testable rules every Use Case Mapping application must enforce, plus a skip-this-methodology fallback. These are HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: Every use-case MUST name ONE primary actor (a role label or persona id) + ≤2 secondary actors. Collective actors — "users", "the team", "we" — are rejected.
rule.rationale: Multi-actor without role separation produces ambiguous responsibility, and a generic actor produces a generic flow; segment-specific flows are what surface segment-specific pain.

rule.statement: Every use-case MUST state the actor's goal in active-verb form as one sentence shaped "[actor] [verb] [object]" ("customer books a flight", "subscriber cancels subscription"). Multi-goal use-cases are split.
rule.rationale: Goal-less use-cases collapse into feature lists with no success criterion; multi-goal use-cases entangle two success criteria in one flow, so neither can be tested cleanly.

rule.statement: Main flow MUST be numbered steps (1..N) with one observable action per step.
rule.rationale: Bulleted prose obscures step boundaries and breaks QA traceability.

rule.statement: Every use-case MUST list ≥1 alternative flow (error, abort) AND ≥1 edge case, each branching from a numbered main-flow step. Main-flow-only use-cases are rejected.
rule.rationale: Single-path use-cases miss the failure modes that drive 80% of bug reports. Separating the alternate flow from the edge case forces the team to surface both the error path and the boundary condition, which are rarely the same thing.

rule.statement: Every use-case MUST end with an observable postcondition (state change, side effect) that doubles as the success criterion QA derives a test from.
rule.rationale: Postcondition is the only thing QA can assert on; a use-case without one is documentation rather than a testable spec.

rule.statement: Every use-case MUST carry an observable trigger — an event, a condition or a time. "When the user wants to …" is rejected.
rule.rationale: Observable triggers map to instrumentation and to a test setup; intent triggers map to nothing, so the use-case cannot be verified in either code or analytics.

rule.statement: If any Applies-If precondition fails OR any Skip-If condition triggers, do NOT apply this methodology. Emit a skip-record naming the failed precondition / triggered skip, and route the task to the correct methodology (or none).
rule.rationale: Mis-application produces worse artefacts than no methodology, because downstream consumers trust the schema; the skip-record makes non-application traceable.
